questions.question: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.questionHtml: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.solution:
Each 1st term square is taken and then subtracted by 1 to get the 2nd term. 

8 : 66 ⇒ (8)2 = 64 - 1 ≠  65. This is an odd one

questions.question: Four number-triads have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-triad that is different.
questions.questionHtml: Four number-triads have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number-triad that is different.
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is;

(First number × 8) + 3 = Second

(Second number × 2) - 3 = Third

1) (10, 77, 151)

10 = First number , 77 = second number , 151 = third number

So, 10 × 8 + 3 = 83

83 × 2  - 3 = 163

So, (10 , 77 , 151 ) ≠ (10 , 83 , 163)

2) (8, 67, 131)

8 × 8 + 3 = 67

67 × 2 - 3 = 131

So, (8, 67, 131) = (8, 67, 131)

3) (4, 35, 67)

8 × 4 + 3 = 35

35 × 2 - 3 = 67

So, (4, 35, 67) = (4, 35, 67)

4) (5, 43, 83)

5× 8 + 3 = 43

43 × 2 - 3 = 83

So, (5, 43, 83) = (5, 43, 83)

Hence, the correct answer is "(10, 77, 151)",
